title: NCL Mine Surveyor Mock 08
pattern: 100 MCQs, 100 marks, 90 min, NO negative marking

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: AutoCAD's 'external reference' (XREF) feature in mine planning allows:
options: Referencing external drawings without embedding them, enabling collaborative work
Neither the first nor the second option
questions.solution: XREF allows referencing external drawings in a master drawing without embedding, enabling collaborative work and easy updates.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: Liscad's 'area calculation' feature computes areas using:
options: Neither the first nor the second option
Both the first and second options
Coordinate geometry methods from boundary coordinates
questions.solution: Liscad computes areas using coordinate geometry methods (like the shoelace formula) from boundary coordinates.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A 3D terrestrial laser scanner works on the principle of:
options: Emitting laser pulses and measuring the time of flight or phase shift of reflected light
questions.solution: 3D laser scanners emit laser pulses and measure the time of flight or phase shift of the reflected light to calculate distance.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: DGPS (Differential GPS) improves accuracy over standard GPS by:
options: Using corrections from a known reference station to eliminate common errors
questions.solution: DGPS uses a base station at a known position to calculate corrections for satellite and atmospheric errors, improving accuracy.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: UAV (Unmanned Aerial Vehicle) photogrammetry in mine surveying involves:
options: Capturing overlapping aerial photographs to create orthophotos and 3D models
questions.solution: UAV photogrammetry captures overlapping aerial photographs processed to create orthophotos, DEMs, and 3D models of mine areas.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'point density' of a 3D laser scanner refers to:
options: The number of points captured per unit area
questions.solution: Point density is the number of 3D points captured per unit area (points/m²), determining the detail level of the scan.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A 'static GPS survey' involves:
options: Occupying fixed points for extended periods (typically 20+ minutes) for high accuracy
questions.solution: Static GPS surveys occupy fixed points for extended periods, allowing long observation times for highest accuracy.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: Dump stability monitoring using a laser scanner helps in:
options: This reverses the cause and effect
Both the first and second options
Detecting surface movements and deformations over time by comparing successive scans
questions.solution: Repeated laser scanning detects surface movements and deformations by comparing successive point clouds, enabling early warning of instability.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A 'LiDAR' sensor mounted on a drone (UAV) provides:
options: This is true only for a different scenario
Neither the first nor the second option
Dense 3D point cloud data of the terrain, penetrating through vegetation
Both the first and second options
questions.solution: Airborne LiDAR provides dense 3D point cloud data that can penetrate vegetation canopy to map the bare ground surface.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'range' of a 3D terrestrial laser scanner refers to:
options: The maximum distance at which it can accurately measure points
The size of the carrying case
questions.solution: Range is the maximum distance at which the scanner can accurately measure, typically 100 m to several hundred metres for mine surveying.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: RTK GPS requires at least how many satellites for centimetre-level accuracy?
questions.solution: RTK GPS requires 5 or more satellites for reliable centimetre-level accuracy and integer ambiguity resolution.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: In drone surveying for mines, the 'ground control points' (GCPs) are used to:
options: Both the first and second options
Provide known reference points for georeferencing and accuracy assessment of aerial photographs
questions.solution: GCPs are ground features with known coordinates used to georeferenced aerial photographs and assess the accuracy of photogrammetric products.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A 'continuous real-time monitoring' system for highwall stability typically uses:
options: Neither the first nor the second option
Both the first and second options
This reverses the cause and effect
Automated sensors (prisms, inclinometers) with data loggers and communication systems
questions.solution: Continuous monitoring uses automated sensors with data loggers and communication systems to provide real-time data on slope movement.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'accuracy' of a 3D laser scanner is typically expressed as:
options: Both the first and second options
This is true only for a different scenario
Neither the first nor the second option
As a function of distance (e.g., ±5 mm at 100 m)
questions.solution: Scanner accuracy is specified as a function of distance, e.g., ±5 mm at 100 m, combining ranging error and angular error.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: DGPS accuracy for mine surveying is typically in the range of:
questions.solution: DGPS typically provides accuracy in the range of 10-50 cm, suitable for general mine surveying but not for high-precision work.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A 'drone (UAV) survey' of a mine area can cover large areas because:
options: Drones can cover large areas quickly with automated flight planning and overlap
Drones can only fly short distances
Drones fly at very low altitude only
questions.solution: Drones with automated flight planning can cover large areas efficiently with programmed routes and required overlap for photogrammetry.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'scan angle' of a 3D terrestrial laser scanner refers to:
options: The angular range over which the scanner can rotate and capture points
questions.solution: The scan angle defines the angular range (e.g., 360° horizontal, 300° vertical) over which the scanner can capture points.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A 'prism-based monitoring system' for dump/highwall stability uses:
options: Both the first and second options
This applies only in specific conditions
Neither the first nor the second option
Automated total stations or laser scanners measuring positions of installed prisms
questions.solution: Prism-based systems use automated total stations or scanners to repeatedly measure positions of prisms installed on the slope surface.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: In RTK GPS surveying, the 'base station' is set up at:
options: A point with known coordinates (or a continuously operating reference station)
questions.solution: The base station is set up at a point with precisely known coordinates, or connected to a CORS network, to provide corrections.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: UAV-based mine surveying typically achieves horizontal accuracy of:
questions.solution: UAV photogrammetry with ground control points typically achieves horizontal accuracy of 2-5 cm, suitable for mine surveying.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'return intensity' of a laser scanner point indicates:
options: The strength of the reflected laser signal, related to surface reflectivity
questions.solution: Return intensity indicates the strength of the reflected laser signal, which depends on surface reflectivity, colour, and angle of incidence.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A 'multi-station' in monitoring refers to:
options: Automated robotic total stations operating continuously without operator intervention
questions.solution: Multi-stations are automated robotic total stations that operate continuously, measuring prism positions at regular intervals without operator.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The main advantage of LiDAR over photogrammetry for mine surveying is:
options: LiDAR can work in any lighting conditions and penetrate vegetation
questions.solution: LiDAR works in any lighting (including night), can penetrate vegetation, and provides direct 3D measurements without needing image matching.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: In drone surveying, 'image overlap' is important because:
options: It ensures sufficient coverage for photogrammetric processing and 3D reconstruction
It only makes the flight longer
questions.solution: Sufficient image overlap (typically 70-80% forward, 60-70% side) ensures photogrammetric software can match features and reconstruct 3D geometry.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A 'deformation monitoring' survey using total stations involves:
options: Both the first and second options
Repeated measurements of the same points over time to detect movements
questions.solution: Deformation monitoring involves repeated measurements of the same points at regular intervals to detect and quantify movements.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'scanning speed' of a 3D laser scanner refers to:
options: The number of points captured per second (e.g., 1 million points/second)
How fast the scanner can be transported
questions.solution: Scanning speed is the rate at which points are captured, measured in points per second (e.g., 1 million pts/sec for modern scanners).

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: GPS 'multipath error' occurs when:
options: GPS signals reflect off nearby surfaces before reaching the receiver
The signal passes through the ionosphere only
questions.solution: Multipath error occurs when GPS signals reflect off nearby surfaces (buildings, ground) before reaching the receiver, causing position errors.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A 'digital zenith camera' in mine surveying is used to determine:
options: Precise astronomical latitude and azimuth by imaging the stars near the zenith
questions.solution: A digital zenith camera images stars near the zenith to determine precise astronomical position and azimuth for high-accuracy orientation.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The 'georeferencing' of drone photographs involves:
options: Both the first and second options
Assigning real-world coordinates to photographs using GCPs or GPS data
Neither the first nor the second option
This is valid only under special circumstances
questions.solution: Georeferencing assigns real-world coordinates to photographs using ground control points or on-board GPS data for spatial accuracy.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A 'total station' used in monitoring for dump stability typically has an angular accuracy of:
questions.solution: Monitoring total stations typically have angular accuracy of ±1" to ±5" (arc-seconds) for precise position measurement.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The process of measuring an angle several times by stacking readings on the circle and dividing by the count is called:
questions.solution: Repetition stacks the angle on the horizontal circle; accumulated reading / repetitions = mean angle.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: In the reiteration (direction) method, angles are derived from:
options: One station to several targets observed sequentially
Both the first and second options
questions.solution: All directions from a single instrument station are observed; angles = difference of directions.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: Temporary adjustments of a theodolite include all EXCEPT:
questions.solution: Collimation error elimination is a permanent (periodic) adjustment, not a field temporary adjustment.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: Centering a theodolite over a station is done with:
questions.solution: Optical plummet or plumb bob positions the vertical axis over the ground mark.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The line of collimation is defined when the telescope is focused on:
questions.solution: Focused at infinity, emerging rays are parallel, defining the line of sight.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: Collimation error means the line of sight is not perpendicular to:
questions.solution: The line of collimation must be perpendicular to the trunnion (horizontal) axis.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: Horizontal axis error means the trunnion axis is not perpendicular to:
questions.solution: The horizontal axis must be perpendicular to the vertical axis for the telescope to sweep a vertical plane.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: Taking Face Left and Face Right readings and averaging eliminates:
options: This applies to a different field entirely
Both collimation and horizontal axis errors
Neither the first nor the second option
questions.solution: Both errors reverse sign on plunge; averaging cancels them.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: Bowditch rule distributes traverse misclosure proportionally to:
questions.solution: Bowditch (compass) rule: correction is proportional to square root of length, assuming comparable angular and linear precision.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: Transit rule distributes linear misclosure proportionally to:
questions.solution: Transit rule: correction to latitude proportional to leg's latitude / total latitude; same for departure.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: Eccentricity of centres is the horizontal offset between:
questions.solution: It is the horizontal displacement of the plumb bob from the true instrument axis.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: Eccentricity of verniers is eliminated by:
options: Reading both A and B plates and taking the mean
questions.solution: Mean of A and B plate readings cancels eccentricity of the graduated circle.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The optical plummet views the ground station through:
options: A small downward-looking eyepiece in the tribrach
questions.solution: Built into the tribrach, it lets the operator verify centering directly.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: Temporary adjustments must be performed at:
options: This is true only for a different scenario
questions.solution: Centering, levelling, and focusing are repeated at every instrument station.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: Levelling screws make the vertical axis:
options: Perpendicular to the line of sight
questions.solution: Foot screws tilt the tribrach until the plate bubble is centred, making the vertical axis vertical.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The plate bubble is used for:
options: Precise levelling along the line of sight
questions.solution: Plate bubble gives rough levelling; the tubular bubble gives precise levelling.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The tubular bubble is more sensitive than the plate bubble because:
options: Larger radius of curvature and longer tube
questions.solution: Sensitivity = 206265 / R; larger R means smaller division value = higher sensitivity.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: Bubble tube sensitivity is given by:
questions.solution: tau = rho / R where rho = 206265 and R is radius of curvature in mm.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The repetition method improves accuracy by:
options: Accumulating angle on circle, averaging reading errors
questions.solution: Accumulation on the circle divides random reading/graduation errors by the repetition count.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: In the repetition method, the number of repetitions should preferably be:
questions.solution: Even repetitions balance Face Left/Face Right use, cancelling instrumental errors.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: After completing repetitions, the mean angle is obtained by:
options: Dividing accumulated reading by number of repetitions
questions.solution: Total accumulated circle reading divided by repetitions = mean angle.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A least count of 20 seconds means the smallest distinguishable reading is:
questions.solution: Least count = smallest angular value reliably readable on the instrument.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: Least count of a vernier theodolite equals:
options: One main scale division / number of vernier divisions
One vernier division / main scale divisions
questions.solution: LC = (value of 1 MSD) / (number of VSD).

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A microptic micrometer achieves least counts of:
questions.solution: Modern microptic theodolites read to 1-5 seconds.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: Plumb bob offset causes the measured horizontal angle to be affected by:
options: Offset direction and distance relative to sighted points
questions.solution: Angular error depends on the geometry: offset magnitude and angle between sight lines.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: Eccentricity of the vertical axis produces maximum angular error when:
options: Observed directions are perpendicular to the offset
questions.solution: Error is proportional to offset x sin(theta); maximum at 90 degrees.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: To reduce plumb bob offset effects, the instrument height should be:
questions.solution: Lower trunnion height reduces the angular effect of any plumb offset.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: Transiting (plunging) the telescope involves:
options: Rotating 180 degrees about the horizontal axis
questions.solution: Plunging flips the telescope end-over-end about the trunnion axis.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: After transiting, the line of collimation sweeps:
questions.solution: With no collimation error, plunging keeps the line of sight in the same vertical plane.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The vertical circle on a modern theodolite reads zero at the:
questions.solution: Zenith distance = 0 degrees when telescope points straight up.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: Vertical circle index error is eliminated by:
options: Taking mean of Face Left and Face Right vertical readings
questions.solution: Index error reverses sign between faces; averaging cancels it.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: Collimation error can be checked by pointing at a distant target, plunging, and backsighting. The observed displacement is:
questions.solution: Displacement after plunge = 2 x collimation error.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: To permanently fix collimation error, the cross-hair is adjusted so the line of sight passes through:
options: The optical centre of objective only
The intersection of horizontal and vertical axes
questions.solution: Collimation adjustment aligns line of sight with the intersection of the trunnion and vertical axes.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: Horizontal axis error causes the telescope to sweep a surface that is:
questions.solution: Non-perpendicular trunnion axis to vertical axis = inclined sweep plane.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: In a closed theodolite traverse, angular misclosure is distributed equally when:
options: All angles are measured with equal precision
questions.solution: Equal-weight angles get equal correction shares.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A precise theodolite traverse in a mine should have angular misclosure not exceeding:
options: plus or minus 10 arcsec root n where n = number of angles
plus or minus 1 arcmin root n
plus or minus 1 degree root n
plus or minus 30 arcsec per angle
questions.solution: Mine survey traverse precision is typically plus or minus 10 arcsec root n for moderate-class work.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: During transport, a theodolite should be carried with the telescope:
questions.solution: Transport with telescope vertical and clamped prevents damage to delicate parts.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The three foot screws of a tribrach should be spread at approximately:
questions.solution: Three screws at 120 degrees provide stable three-point support for levelling.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: Reiteration is preferred over repetition when:
options: Many directions are observed from one station
Both the first and second options
High accuracy needed for single angle
questions.solution: Reiteration is efficient when multiple directions radiate from one station.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The included angle at a station is computed by:
options: Subtracting the back direction from the forward direction
questions.solution: Included angle = forward direction minus back direction (reduced to same face).

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A 1 arcsec theodolite circle typically has main scale divisions of:
questions.solution: Main scale divisions of 1 degree subdivided by micrometer to read 1 arcsec.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The tangent screw of a theodolite provides:
questions.solution: Tangent screw moves the telescope slowly for precise pointing after the clamp is engaged.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: Cross-hairs are located at:
options: At the centre of the telescope tube
The focal plane of the objective
questions.solution: Cross-hairs are placed at the focal plane so both target image and cross-hair are in focus together.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: When the telescope is focused at infinity, the image of a distant target forms at:
options: The cross-hair plane only if adjusted
The focal plane of the objective
questions.solution: Parallel rays from infinity converge at the focal plane of the objective.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A theodolite is levelled when the plate bubble is:
options: Central in both positions of the plate tube
At one end of the tube
questions.solution: Bubble must be central when the plate tube is viewed parallel and perpendicular to a pair of foot screws.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The optical plummet is checked for accuracy by:
options: Rotating it 180 degrees and checking if the mark stays centred
questions.solution: Rotate the optical plummet 180 degrees; if the mark shifts, the plummet needs adjustment.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: In Face Left position, the vertical circle is on the:
questions.solution: Face Left = vertical circle on the left (observer's left when viewing through telescope).

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: In Face Right position, the vertical circle is on the:
questions.solution: Face Right = vertical circle on the right, achieved by plunging and rotating 180 degrees.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: A total station combines the functions of a theodolite and:
questions.solution: A total station integrates an electronic theodolite, EDM, and on-board computer.

questions.subject: Mine Surveying
questions.stem: The coordinate measurement mode of a total station determines:
options: X, Y, Z coordinates of the target point
questions.solution: Coordinate mode uses measured angle, distance, and known station data to compute 3D coordinates.

questions.solution: World Water Day is observed on 22 March.

questions.solution: Nifty 50 is the benchmark index of the National Stock Exchange (NSE).

questions.solution: Ahmedabad is known as the Manchester of India due to its textile industry.

questions.solution: GST was implemented on 1 July 2017.

questions.solution: Shaktikanta Das is the Governor of RBI.

questions.stem: Which metal's price determines the health of the Indian economy's industrial sector?
questions.solution: Copper is considered a barometer of economic/industrial health.

questions.solution: Petroleum products are India's largest export by value.

questions.subject: General Awareness

questions.solution: India's first bullet train project connects Mumbai and Ahmedabad.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: Who was the first Indian woman to go to space?
questions.solution: Kalpana Chawla was the first Indian-born woman in space (1997).

questions.stem: The National Stock Exchange (NSE) was established in which year?
questions.solution: NSE was established in 1992 and commenced operations in 1994.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: India's largest commercial bank by assets is:
questions.solution: SBI is India's largest commercial bank by assets.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: Which index measures inflation based on wholesale prices?
questions.solution: WPI (Wholesale Price Index) measures wholesale price inflation.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: Choose the synonym of 'BENEVOLENT':
questions.solution: Benevolent means kind and generous.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: Choose the antonym of 'TRANSPARENT':
questions.solution: Opaque is the antonym of transparent.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: Choose the synonym of 'DILIGENT':
questions.solution: Diligent means showing care and effort (hardworking).

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: Choose the antonym of 'ABUNDANT':
questions.solution: Scarce is the antonym of abundant.

questions.subject: Technical (Mining)
questions.stem: The ratio of three numbers is 2:3:4. The sum of the largest and smallest equals the middle number increased by 14. What is the smallest number?
questions.solution: Numbers: 2x, 3x, 4x. 4x + 2x = 3x + 14 → 3x = 14 → x = 14/3. Smallest = 28/3. Not matching... Let me reconsider. Maybe: 2x + 4x = 3x + 14 → 3x = 14 → x ≈ 4.67. Smallest = 9.33. Still not matching. Perhaps the sum equals the middle + 14: 2x+4x = 3x+14 → x=14/3. Not an integer.

questions.subject: Technical (Mining)
questions.stem: Two successive discounts of 10% and 20% are equivalent to a single discount of:

questions.subject: Technical (Mining)
questions.stem: Two cars start from the same point at 50 km/h and 60 km/h in opposite directions. After how many hours will they be 330 km apart?
questions.solution: Relative speed = 110 km/h. Time = 330/110 = 3 hours

questions.subject: Technical (Mining)
questions.stem: If 3A = 4B = 5C, what is A:B:C?
